short: The first tank in service with Chobham armour, and the longest recorded tank kill.
full:
Challenger 1 began as the Shir 2, designed for the Shah of Iran; when the 1979 revolution cancelled the order Britain took the design on to replace ageing Chieftains, and it entered service in 1983. It was the first tank in service to use Chobham composite armour, and a Rolls-Royce CV12 engine cured the mobility problems of its predecessor. Its 120 mm L11 rifled gun and fire-control system were largely inherited, and its crews performed poorly at the 1987 Canadian Army Trophy gunnery competition, which caused some public embarrassment.

The Gulf War in 1991 went better. The 176 Challengers of 1st Armoured Division destroyed around 300 Iraqi armoured vehicles without loss to enemy fire, and one is credited with the longest confirmed tank-against-tank kill, at roughly 5,100 metres. Challenger 1 left British service in 2001 as Challenger 2 arrived; several hundred went to Jordan, which rebuilt them as the Al-Hussein and began retiring them in 2018.
